newsitem.title: USA: Fed expected to refrain from open market operation.
newsitem.headline: Fed expected to refrain from open market operation.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is likely to refrain from open market operations on Friday, analysts said.
Analysts said the banking systems need for reserves had been met by the Fed's temporary addition of reserves on Thursday through seven-day fixed system repurchase agreements.
"I'm looking for no Fed today," said Patricia Thrapp, vice president at Aubrey G. Lanston & Co. Inc. "I think the seven-day system (that the Fed conducted on Thursday) will satisfy the add need."
Thrapp said the Treasury's deposits at the Fed would climb after the weekend, draining reserves from the banking system and creating a need for more additions of reserves next week.
"And there continues to be a possibility of outright purchases by the Fed," she said.
Fed funds were trading at 5-7/16 percent, below the Fed's 5-1/2 percent target for the rate, at mid-morning.
